results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 67 aligned summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order; the three callouts are apparatus (null). Eva ¶1's summary ('walkthrough setup: hosted checkout with two sanctioned extensions') stresses the extensions, but the paragraph introduces the step-by-step walkthrough whose table carries the calls and answers, so it matches p50.

Cart ¶2, the only unit marked two_ideas (the cart as a non-reserving draft / reserve-on-add), holds one controlling idea as declared in p11: reserve-on-add is the 'reserves no stock' property stated as the first business decision.
Every unit ties to a supporting claim S1-S6 or is intro, conclusion or transition apparatus.

results.quote: Visa's May 2025 monitoring fact sheet tracks these enumeration attacks, bots trying card numbers one after another, separately from disputes.
results.finding: The Visa source is cited but no sentence says what it shows for the argument (the spec's 'shows': documented symptoms and controls); flow reader B (item 17) could not see what it adds.

All other evidence is explained: both tables in 'What Checkout Must Call' are followed by what they show; the Baymard, Mollie, Stripe, Apple Pay, Shop Pay, Shopify changelog and PCI DSS items each carry a sentence of interpretation; the Eva table is read by 'Three details of this order matter'; the four-options table summarizes option paragraphs that each explain their row; the stage table is read by the paragraph that carries it.

results.quote: The chapter starts from three requests Kestrel & Pine's head of engineering receives about its checkout.
results.finding: Declared: sequence, carrying over Eva's order created at 21:14 with payment pending and introducing the order in which the chapter explains how that happens. The roadmap opens cold after the Eva paragraph and does not pick up her order or say the chapter will explain how it came about.

results.quote: At the start of this chapter a price changed, another customer bought the last item and the payment answer arrived late while a shopper checked out.
results.finding: Declared: conclusion_summary carrying over 'Kestrel & Pine's checkout kept, with what it calls changed' (the end of the stage section). The conclusion goes straight to the opening's three changes and does not pick up the kept checkout. The callback is met; the carried-over information is not.

All other boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information, read in the current section order (scene, cart-draft, calls, clock, eva, guest-wallets, b2b, wrong, abandoned, choices, shopify, stages): e.g. 'What checkout writes, every later system inherits', 'That short-lived state cannot last long', 'The two rules are easiest to see on one order', 'Eva signed in, but no shopper has to', 'A business customer changes more than a guest or a wallet does', 'Whoever the buyer, the calls fail in the same ways', 'Milan's other two requests...', 'Option 2 gives the merchant only what the platform allows'.
Opens on the declared puzzling scenario; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

Opens with synthesis, not 'in conclusion'; the Established / Depends on context / author's synthesis lists sort the findings by how settled they are rather than restating them; no new idea (Bancontact appears as a new example only, see flow).

¶1 states what no section states alone: the same need (one order created once at peak, with card numbers typed into it) explains both the two rules and the platform's limits, so the merchant's decision is which owner answers each call and which sanctioned mechanism carries each change; the questions turn it into action.
¶1 returns to the opening shopper's price change, last item and late payment answer and says what keeps each from breaking the order.

Both readers describe the declared organisation: concepts, mechanism, worked example, variants, failures, then the who-may-change-checkout half driven by Milan's requests (prerequisite order with problem_solution and comparison). No section is 'unclear' to either; Abandoned Carts is 'only partly clear' to both. Not counted as material: W1/W2/W4, ERP/WMS, webhook and the 2026 incident names (A2, A9, B8, B13), which the spec's audience already knows from earlier chapters.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Kestrel & Pine: Three Requests for the Checkout ¶1
results.quote: In her second month, Noor Visser gets three requests about the same page.
results.finding: Noor appears by name without being tied to the 'head of engineering' of the roadmap, and 'second month' has no reference; both readers had to infer who she is (A1: 'Noor first named; roadmap only said head of engineering').

results.quote: The first is the **shopper's patience**.
results.finding: The evidence for the 'patience clock' is a list of abandonment reasons, mostly not about time, and the same content returns in Abandoned Carts and in guest checkout (A4: 'Not a time limit; a list of abandonment reasons; anticipates the Abandoned Carts section'). Both readers propose moving it to Abandoned Carts; the placement is the spec's (p19 under the clock section).

results.quote: A card authorization, the bank's reservation of the amount, is valid for days once granted (the PSPs Stripe and Adyen list 5 to 7 days for most card schemes, the networks such as Visa and Mastercard).
results.finding: Nested parentheses, glosses and citations split subject from verb in this paragraph; both readers re-read (A5 on the Mollie sentence, A6: 'Another nested gloss; capture vs authorization introduced in passing').

results.quote: **Creating the order once despite retries.**
results.finding: After 'Two rules follow.' the first rule is labelled with a noun phrase while the second is an imperative, so it did not read as a rule (A7).

results.quote: Since early 2027 two apps, Kestrel & Pine's answer to Milan's requests, add to it through the platform's sanctioned extension points
results.finding: Gives away how Milan's requests were resolved long before the sections that answer them and forces the reader to sort out the timeline (A3). The extensions belong in Eva's order (p50); calling them 'the answer to Milan's requests' here is the draft's choice.

results.quote: checkout reads the shop platform's hourly copy from the ERP, itself fed every 15 minutes by the WMS.
results.finding: An hourly copy fed every 15 minutes does not add up to the 'up to two hours old' stated elsewhere; both readers could not reconcile it (A8).

results.quote: the delivery date still comes from a fixed rule
results.finding: With a delivery-date extension already in place, the reader could not tell whether Milan's delivery-date request succeeded or failed, and the later 'Milan's two requests end there' does not reconcile the weakness (A10).

results.quote: Daniel's question is now answerable.
results.finding: Separated from the stock weakness it resolves by the delivery-date paragraph and Figure 5 (B12). The figure is attached to p53 by the spec.

results.finding: 'One of the two' is ambiguous, and Sanne asked checkout to stop creating unpaid orders while the design keeps creating pending ones; the request is reframed without saying so (A12).

The intro reader predicted every section in order (scene, cart/checkout/order, calls and freshness, clocks and detour, Eva, guest/wallets/business buyers, five failures, abandoned carts, four ways, Shopify 2023-2026, scale stages), the evidence (Kestrel & Pine's checkout and incidents, vendor documentation, Baymard, Shopify's changelog) and the tone. It noted that 'three requests' sits oddly beside 'the storefront owner's requests' spanning four sections.

Matches expected: order created once with payment pending, keyed on cart and payment, not the thank-you page; marked paid only by the provider's signed webhook; the repeat changes nothing because event ids are recorded; daily job after the expiry window. The reader noted a gap: Eva's table places order creation at 'Confirmation' 21:14, after the 21:13 redirect, without saying what creates the order if she never returns.

Matches expected: fault in the platform's stock copy (up to two hours old) that answered the availability call; checkout owns no facts; fix in who answers the call (W1 availability service), not in checkout.

Matches expected: use sanctioned extension points (time budgets, versioned); PCI DSS 6.4.3/11.6.1 script rules and a skimmer reading every card; Shopify's dated withdrawal of checkout.liquid, additional scripts and Scripts; keep an inventory with mechanism and support date.

results.quote: Seconds, plus the authentication detour
results.finding: The freshness table's Payment row uses 'the authentication detour' (3-D Secure / strong customer authentication, on does_not_know) one section before the clock section explains it (terms reader item 13).

results.quote: Kestrel & Pine runs the shop platform's hosted checkout.
results.finding: 'Hosted checkout' is on does_not_know; it is used here without a gloss and explained only in the four-options section (option 1) (terms reader item 18).

results.draft_locus: Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits ¶1
results.quote: a plan-tier gate blocks a needed change
results.finding: The stage table's warning sign 'plan-tier gate' is never explained (presumably a feature limited to a higher plan, such as Shopify Plus) (terms reader item 35).

Every does_not_know term is given in the draft (cart/checkout/order, reserve-on-add, payment session, detour, 3-D Secure and SCA, idempotency key, webhook as external truth, guest checkout, express wallet, payment token, conversion, abandoned cart, company account, contract price list, reverse charge, payment terms, credit check, extension point, time budget, headless, PCI DSS and its questionnaire, sandboxed function); apart from the four failures, each is given at or before first use in the body. Terms the reader flagged that the audience already knows are not failures: webhook, ERP, WMS, B2B, PSP, idempotency/'idempotent per order', committing stock, the ledger and order management, the scale stages and Omnichannel, Waypoint W1/W2/W4 and the availability service, Noor and the other people, the Card-Testing Night and the Black Friday Oversell. Plain or incidental words (tax engine, storefront, fulfill, checkout session after the payment session, callback, payment sheet, net 30, disputes, Cyber Monday, Ruby, PostNL, open-source cores, asynchronous methods) are not counted; paragraph openings B1-B6 start from known people, systems or stages. Noor's role and the stage-2/option-2 confusion are recorded under flow_is_followable.
